the high-order FD schemes can be accelerated effectively using the proposed FPGA-based hardware architecture design.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high-order finite difference scheme can greatly improve the efficiency of simulating linear acoustic wave propagation problems.

our FPGA-based hardware implementation can achieve 7~20x speedup over its pure software counterpart for 2-order accurate finite difference algorithm, while the speedup is proportional to the number of spatial grid points.

the proposed FPGA-based hardware accelerator can be used as a general-purpose reconfigurable coprocessing platform to speed up high-order finite difference time domain simulations of wave propagation problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we proposed a novel memory architecture design and its efficient FPGA implementation to accelerate the high-order finite difference algorithm for simulating acoustic wave propagation phenomena in 2D and 3D space with high computational efficiency.
we have developed an FPGA-based high-order finite difference algorithm to accelerate the 2D acoustic wave propagation problems.
, by adopting high-order FD operators in both space and time, we can reduce the number of spatial grid points and time steps required to simulate acoustic waves over long distances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can achieve high computational speed using a reconfigurable hardware platform with a moderate number of FPGA logic resources.
we can use a single FPGA chip to accelerate a 3D simulation problem by integrating multiple FPGA chips together.
the memory architecture design for high-order FD numerical schemes can be extended to other time domain simulation tasks, such as computational electromagnetic applications.
